title: Moneygo #22 bounded refund receipt coordinator contract
description: Design only. Structural schema plus mandatory semantic rules; this file is not an implementation or persisted-data schema. All newly owned object fields are closed. Legacy proof leaves are closed by their existing authoritative validators and exact-source equality, not by an invented mirror schema. JSON schema alone does not validate a ticket or authorize a write.

month.x-semantic-validator: month of a valid source civil date

timestamp.x-semantic-validator: Valid civil date, finite instant, exact toISOString round trip

reason.x-semantic-validator: Nonempty after trim; normalize exactly Relations.allocateRefund reason() and show normalized final reason

plainData.x-use: Output-only exact legacy snapshots; never a new free-form API field or accepted caller proof

oneOf.x-selection: transactions and selected linked active source rows
exact cash, personal, accountFlows, accountBalances and selected drilldown rows specified by effects closure

createCoordinator(capabilities).semantics: Host-owned zero-argument functions; no user-overridable state, writer, storage, date argument or public test seam. Fixed production dependencies. Callbacks are the sole non-JSON input exception.

inspect(raw,selection).purpose: Complete readonly proof for any extant chosen income, including every blocked row; cannot authorize allocation.

commit(raw,ticket,confirmation).result: Frozen complete Ledger.validateState-valid candidate state, not persisted; maximum 32 MiB ledger. Its rebuilt review must fit 8 MiB. Host owns saving.
commit(raw,ticket,confirmation).mutation: Consumes recognized ticket before any validation failure; returned candidate alone is not success

isCurrent(raw,ticket).mutation: Nonconsuming; false must make UI retire consent; detects observed clock rollback and stale raw/validated basis

cancel(ticket).mutation: Idempotent private invalidation, no ledger write

invalidateAll().mutation: Increment private generation and retire tickets, no ledger write

x-limits.boundaryRule: Exact boundary passes only if the whole inherited state/proof also validates; one-over fails before write. No silent truncation. Report byte count is canonical JSON UTF-8 without whitespace.

x-semantic-rules: All JSON inputs require descriptor-first ordinary-data capture before getters, serialization, validator calls or finance. Cross-realm plain objects/arrays supported; reject accessors, symbols, cycles, custom prototypes/toJSON, array holes/extras, nonfinite/unsafe integers; fail safely on proxies or hostile thrown errors.

Full raw canonical binding preserves absence versus explicit values, array order, every source/history field; object key insertion order is immaterial. Also bind full validated state. Retained-identity side metadata must be reconstructed by the existing validator/writer, never dropped or invented.

Only current host civil date accepted; no asOf input. Samples before/after each operation; date stable throughout and since preview; instant nondecreasing within operation and relative to prior observation. No timeout or unobservable clock-history claim.

E = expected; L = all linked; R = linked with income date <= today; F = L-R; U=E-R; P=E-L. Enforce R+F=L, U=P+F, 0<=L<=E, X>=0 with BigInt accumulation. none/partial/full uses R against E. due<today is past; needsCheck exactly waiting && U>0 && known due<today.

Capacity uses Relations.calculate current impacts. Plan capacity null means not applicable only. Eligible iff no blocking reasons and min(receipt, expense, optional plan)>0. Blocked maxAllocatableCents is zero. Plan status is never a blocking reason. Wrong/missing IDs, wrong transaction types and mismatched plan/expense reject the query/selection instead of inventing a row.

Candidate classification and literal case-insensitive search filter only after complete scan/ranking. Search fields are ID, date, note, account name/ID, confirmed merchant and indexed source key/stable ID. No fuzzy matching, source-note merchant fallback, regex execution or arbitrary lookback. Count semantics: eligible+blocked=scanned; matching is after classification+search; rows is matching slice; nextOffset is null exactly at exhaustion; offset beyond end returns empty page.

Rank eligible and blocked views by the same stable tuple: confirmed nonempty merchant match desc, available amount == P desc when P>0, same account desc, absolute civil-day distance asc, receipt date asc, ID code-unit asc. Unknown match is null, sorts as false, never equals unknown. SubstantiveTieCount is measured over the same classification population before search and paging on the first four facts; no tie creates consent. Exact-amount fact null without a positive plan cap.

Every proofRef resolves exactly once inside this immutable proof; no duplicate or dangling reference; no live mutable drilldown as a substitute. Proof entry values must equal complete existing-authority snapshots for their kind, phase and sourcePath. Snapshot leaves are not extensible bags; unknown keys rejected by the relevant existing schema and state validation. Public API view snapshots must equal freshly produced complete rows.

Closure includes selected source transactions/accounts/categories/profiles; canonical duplicate links and linked source snapshots; all own and linked import evidence plus referenced first/last batches; confirmed canonical merchant row and its application batch; applicable coverage declarations with unknown completeness; relevant held/composite/transfer exclusion proofs. No merchant from a shadow becomes the canonical match.

Capacity closure includes every active refund/settlement consuming selected income, every refund/claim consuming selected expense, every refund linked to selected plan, their endpoint transaction signatures/snapshots and linked receipt dates. Store each record once per phase and reference it in all relevant groups. Never sum a duplicated reference twice.

Planning closure compares complete public before/after view rows for all existing attributions, selects every changed attribution plus selected-source attributions and their plan/source rows, includes stored proof records and dependent plan attributions needed to explain totals. Respect unsupported/unknown proof states. No planning reservation is subtracted from refund capacity. Missing modules or incomplete proof block preview.

Effects include exact Relations.calculate all-date and unique expense/receipt month totals, unchanged per-account balances and full selected source account-flow legs. Preserve all existing old closes and expose IDs in affected months. Do not recompute forecasts or rewrite frozen closes.

Only unchanged public allocateRefund constructs preview/replay candidates. After confirming exactly one new refund and one matching create/refund audit, correct fresh IDs/revision/reason/signatures, and refund.createdAt == audit.at == audit.after.createdAt, compare candidate states masking only /bookkeeping/refunds/<new-index>/createdAt, /bookkeeping/audit/<new-index>/at and /bookkeeping/audit/<new-index>/after/createdAt. Prior rows/timestamps and all other bytes remain exact. Compare reviews deterministically derived from those already-checked masked candidates; do not mask additional independently supplied review fields.

Output is detached and deeply frozen. Ticket identity is private WeakMap authority; reconstructed JSON, copied/foreign ticket, caller-mutated review, or raw supplied candidate has no authority. Recognized commit attempt consumes identity even on malformed consent, stale state, clock failure, writer/replay error or host save failure.

Host raw storage-byte guard remains independent. Host may retry exactly the same returned candidate once for existing optional-history quota cleanup. Never rerun commit for save retry, never show success or discard draft until change() returns true.

Lifecycle invalidations are mandatory: draft edits, close/Escape/backdrop/back-to-draft, target switch/new dialog, live details/navigation/pagehide/BFCache, restore/reset, unrelated save, storage conflict, stale currentness and runtime disposal. Immutable-review-only paging/search may retain ticket; draft or navigation changes cannot.

No overview/candidate/inspection/preview failure changes caller state or storage; no persisted review/ticket/rank/rejection registry, dependency, version, storage key, income row, payment or automatic lifecycle change is introduced. Core schemas and public allocator remain byte-identical.

Overview and candidate-page summary scopes/warnings have empty proofRefs by schema; their evidence/record IDs are summaries only. Full scoped coverage declaration references and proof-bearing warnings exist only in inspect/review, whose immutable proof registries must resolve them. No summary claims an absent full proof.

x-error-policy.candidateReasons: Stable explanations; not a promise of downstream error ordering or code equality. Historical audit errors can precede role-specific errors.
x-error-policy.writer: Actual writer remains authoritative. RR_WRITER_REJECTED may expose a bounded own-data downstreamCode/message only; hostile errors use a generic safe message.
x-error-policy.invalidTicket: No identity recognized means nothing consumed; a recognized ticket is consumed before malformed confirmation is reported.
x-error-policy.inputMutation: Every failure is atomic with respect to caller state and stored financial bytes.
